scores.evidence: LLM guardrail check before any agent action: if text matches jailbreak patterns (e.g., "ignore previous instructions"), escalate to human and log.
scores.rationale: Pattern-matching as the injection defense is weak and called an "LLM guard"; also webhook "30 sec timeout" with synchronous LLM, ngrok for GitHub App, and "localhost:8000" claims are shaky, and auto-close policy relies on model confidence.

scores.evidence: Phase 3: no auto-fixes (too risky); humans do all resolution.
scores.rationale: The request asks for an agent that resolves issues; the plan is a triage/labeling/dup-closing bot with no reproduction, code fix or PR capability, deferring remediation entirely.

scores.evidence: Async batch review (nightly cron, human reviews pending actions...) vs. Phase 0 agent posts label+comment immediately
scores.rationale: Mostly consistent phases, but contradictions exist: batch approval before posting versus immediate posting and auto-close, 'stateless' vs dead-letter queue, and duplicate detection via semantic search while vector store is deferred.

scores.evidence: Randomly sample 50 real GitHub issues from production backlog... Run agent on each issue in dry-run mode... Duplicate precision: ≥95%.
scores.rationale: Gated, staged offline/backtest validation with checkable thresholds and ongoing audits, though sample sizes are small, thresholds are invented, and injection testing is thin.

scores.evidence: ASSUMPTION: $0.01–$0.05 per triage + $0.02–$0.10 per resolution attempt (GPT-4o or similar)
scores.rationale: Many figures are labeled assumptions and missing inputs noted, but numerous thresholds (85%, 95%, $100/month) are stated as requirements without basis and sensitivity is partial.

scores.evidence: Inference endpoint failure: agent logs error, escalates issue to human queue (backlog), does not retry (avoid infinite loops).
scores.rationale: Covers endpoint failures, 429s, false closes and injection, but misses bot loops, webhook duplicates/idempotency, concurrent edits, and sandbox issues.

scores.evidence: Circuit breaker: if error rate >5% for >10 min, shut down webhook + page on-call.
scores.rationale: Rollback, alerts, runbook, cost alerts and circuit breaker are present; Phase 0 deployment on localhost/ngrok and ownership details are thin.

scores.evidence: daily budget alert if spend exceeds $10; hard halt if >$20 (pilot phase).
scores.rationale: Token caps, daily spend halts, per-issue cost tracking and monthly targets exist, though no estimate for resolution cost, and figures are loosely grounded.

scores.evidence: R3 (once agent closes even 10 real issues, reverting trust requires audit...)
scores.rationale: Decisions are explicitly classified by reversibility with revisit triggers and deferrals, though the classification is partly odd (model choice, approval flow) and misses identity/data model issues.

scores.evidence: Simple state machine: webhook → ingest → classify → label (if confidence >70%) OR escalate
scores.rationale: Starts simple and defers vector store, fine-tuning, and ensembles, but has heavy process ceremony and under-builds the resolution core.

scores.evidence: Scaffold GitHub App (webhook receiver, OAuth token refresh). Implement classifier prompt: issue → category + confidence JSON.
scores.rationale: Phased tasks with concrete exit checks and gating are actionable for triage, but there's nothing to act on for the resolution component.

checklist.evidence: Phase 1: agent triages only (labels + comments). Phase 2b: unlock close on high-confidence duplicates and spam
GitHub token scoped to read-only labels (no delete).
Data (no code path): issue titles, bodies, and comments are treated as untrusted user input.
Phase 3: no auto-fixes (too risky); humans do all resolution.
Randomly sample 50 real GitHub issues from production backlog... Run agent on each issue in dry-run mode
Track human override rate: measure % of agent labels / comments rejected by team; target <10%.
Hard stop at token cap; circuit breaker: if error rate >5% for >10 min, shut down webhook + page on-call.
Fixed 1,000 output tokens per issue... daily budget alert if spend exceeds $10; hard halt if >$20
Add close action audit: log every close + reason (for incident postmortem).
Stateless design: agent does not retain conversation history across issues.

traps.evidence: Phase 3: no auto-fixes (too risky); humans do all resolution.
issue titles, bodies, and comments are treated as untrusted user input.
Sustained ≥85% accuracy (match to final human decision or resolution).
Hard stop at token cap; if exceeded, agent logs and escalates to human without completing action.

note: Well-gated, carefully phased triage-labeling bot with real validation, but it drops the resolution half of the request, and its injection defense is pattern matching with no sandbox, PR flow, idempotency, or loop handling.
